newsitem.title: INDIA: Central bank policy gives Delhi shares a lift.
newsitem.headline: Central bank policy gives Delhi shares a lift.

text.p: Delhi share prices surged in afternoon trade on Thursday, boosted by the central bank's half-yearly credit policy announced earlier in the week, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index was up 6.05 points at 766.68 at 12:45 p.m. (0715 GMT).
"Marketmen are expecting a substantial increase in the liquidity following the Reserve Bank policy," said one broker.
The Reserve Bank of India on Tuesday announced its six-month policy beginning on April 1, aimed at bringing down banks' lending rates and increasing liquidity in the money market.
Stock markets were closed on Wednesday for the Hindu festival Ramnavami.
Traders said political uncertainty kept a lid on the rally.
"The share prices would have shot up sharply but the political scenario forced operators to adopt a cautious approach," said Vijay Aggarwal of brokers Mass Financial Services.

India's search for a new leader to end a 19-day political crisis was delayed on Thursday as the ousted United Front coalition postponed a decision on who would replace caretaker Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda.

United Front officials said the decision was postponed due to political infighting and the death of veteran party boss Biju Patnaik. The front's Steering Committee was expected to try to take a decision on Friday.
Reliance Industries gained 7.75 rupees to 275.50 as speculators bought on expectations the company would declare strong results for 1996/97 (April-March), to be announced on April 22, brokers said.
State Bank of India rose 10.40 rupees to 296.40 on foreign buying.
Larsen and Toubro edged up 3.25 rupees 216.10.
